docs/architecture.html.title: Architecture | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/architecture.html.summary: Architecture MyAgents Community separates agent definitions from provider integration, execution, and state persistence. flowchart LR App[Application] --> Factory[IAgentSessionFactory] Factory --> Session[Agent session] Definition[AgentDefinition and features] --> Assembly[Agent assembly: prompts, tools, capabilities] Assembly --> Session Session --> Runtime[MyAgents.Runtime.Chat] Runtime <--> Client[Microsoft.Extensions.AI IChatClient] Client --> Provider[Provider and model] Runtime --> Policy[IToolApprovalPolicy] Policy --> Tools[Registered ITool implementations] Runtime --> Observers[Tool observers] Integrations[Memory and MCP integrations] -. optional features .-> Definition Core Abstractions AgentDefinition & Features An agent is defined declaratively using AgentDefinition composed of one or more IAgentFeature instances. Features contribute: System Prompts: Contextual prompts, role definitions, and guidelines. Tools: In-process delegate tools, generated [AgentTool] wrappers, or MCP tool proxies. Capabilities: Structured output schemas, streaming controls, and model options. IAgentSession & Factory IAgentSessionFactory builds an executable IAgentSession bound to an isolated session identifier and conversation state. The session manages chat history and exposes InvokeAsync for conversational turns. ChatClientRuntime The chat runtime (MyAgents.Runtime.Chat) manages the interaction with IChatClient: Dispatches model requests. Parses tool calls requested by the model. Evaluates configured IToolApprovalPolicy policies. Invokes approved tools and feeds results back to the model turn loop until completion. Streams token deltas incrementally while preserving whole-turn guardrails.

docs/durable-runs.html.title: Durable Agent Runs | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/durable-runs.html.summary: Durable Agent Runs MyAgents.Runtime.Workers and MyAgents.Runtime.Workers.Sqlite enable durable, restart-recoverable agent workloads using standard .NET Generic Host worker patterns. Architecture flowchart TD Client[Submit Request] --> Backend[IAgentRunBackend (Sqlite)] Backend --> Queue[(Persisted Runs Table)] WorkerService[AgentRunWorkerService] --> Lease[Acquire Lease] Queue --> Lease Lease --> Handler[IAgentRunHandler] Handler --> Result[AgentRunHandlerResult] Result --> Complete[Mark Completed / Failed] Complete --> Queue Setup Configure the durable worker with SQLite persistence: using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection; using Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting; using MyAgents.Core.Execution; using MyAgents.Runtime.Workers; using MyAgents.Runtime.Workers.Sqlite; var builder = Host.CreateApplicationBuilder(); // 1. Register the SQLite run backend builder.Services.AddSingleton<IAgentRunBackend>(_ => new SqliteAgentRunBackend("agent-runs.db")); // 2. Register your custom run handler builder.Services.AddSingleton<IAgentRunHandler, MyDurableAgentHandler>(); // 3. Register the background worker service builder.Services.AddMyAgentsRunWorker(options => { options.IdlePollInterval = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(250); options.LeaseDuration = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30); options.LeaseRenewalInterval = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10); options.BaseRetryDelay = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(2); options.MaximumRetryDelay = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5); }); using var host = builder.Build(); await host.RunAsync(); Submitting a Run Runs can be submitted from any web API or CLI client: var backend = host.Services.GetRequiredService<IAgentRunBackend>(); var request = new AgentRunRequest( HandlerId: "research-assistant", InputJson: """{"topic": "Quantum Computing", "depth": "advanced"}""", IdempotencyKey: "run-query-101", ScopeKey: "user-42" ); var submission = await backend.SubmitAsync(request); Console.WriteLine($"Run {submission.RunId} submitted. Deduplicated: {submission.WasDeduplicated}"); If the hosting process crashes or is restarted during execution, the active lease expires and another worker automatically reclaims the run and resumes execution.

docs/hybrid-rag.html.title: Hybrid RAG & Memory | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/hybrid-rag.html.summary: Hybrid RAG & Memory MyAgents.Memory provides a complete retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system with zero external vendor SDK dependencies. Key Capabilities Hybrid Retrieval: Combines SIMD dense cosine similarity (TensorPrimitives.Dot) with BM25 sparse lexical ranking via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF). Zero-Dependency Document Readers: Ingest HTML, Markdown, Plain Text, and JSON streams directly without third-party parser dependencies. Reactive Index Synchronization: Uses IMemoryStoreChangeNotifier to keep the BM25 lexical index in sync automatically when vector records change. Grounded Citations: Formats citations ([1], [2]), enforces token context budgets, expands adjacent chunk windows, and verifies factual grounding. Configuration using Microsoft.Extensions.AI; using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection; using MyAgents.Memory; using MyAgents.Memory.Ingestion; var services = new ServiceCollection(); // 1. Register vector store (SqliteMemoryStore, VectorMemoryStore, or VectorDataMemoryStore) services.AddSingleton<IMemoryStore>(sp => new SqliteMemoryStore("memory.db", sp.GetRequiredService<IEmbeddingGenerator<string, Embedding<float>>>())); // 2. Register document ingestion with markdown chunking services.AddDocumentIngestion(builder => { builder.WithChunkingOptions(new TextChunkingOptions(ChunkSize: 1000, ChunkOverlap: 100)); builder.UseMarkdownChunker(); }); Document Ingestion Ingest files or streams with automatic title extraction and format detection: var ingestor = provider.GetRequiredService<IDocumentIngestor>(); // Ingest an HTML or Markdown file directly await ingestor.IngestFileAsync( "knowledge/architecture-guide.html", cancellationToken: cancellationToken); Grounded Citation Feature Add RetrievalAugmentationFeature to your agent definition to inject relevant context messages and verify model references: var ragFeature = new RetrievalAugmentationFeature(retriever, new RetrievalAugmentationOptions { MaxResults = 5, MaxContextTokens = 1500, AdjacentChunkWindow = 1, AppendCitationReferences = true }); var definition = new AgentDefinition("grounded-assistant", [ragFeature]);

docs/nativeaot-tools.html.title: NativeAOT Tools | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/nativeaot-tools.html.summary: NativeAOT Tools MyAgents.Generators provides a Roslyn incremental source generator that analyzes [AgentTool] attributes on static or instance methods. Why NativeAOT Tools? In traditional frameworks, tool invocation relies heavily on runtime reflection and runtime JSON schema generation via System.Text.Json reflection. This causes: Startup latency and JIT compilation overhead. High memory allocations on every tool call. Incompatibility with .NET NativeAOT compilation and trimming. With MyAgents.Generators, all JSON schemas and argument bindings are evaluated at compile time. Authoring an [AgentTool] To author a NativeAOT-safe tool: Define your parameter and return records. Create a JsonSerializerContext referencing the types. Annotate the tool method with [AgentTool]: using System.ComponentModel; using System.Text.Json.Serialization; using MyAgents.Core.Tools; public sealed record SupportTicket(string Subject, int Priority = 3); public sealed record TicketResult(int Id, string Status); [JsonSerializable(typeof(SupportTicket))] [JsonSerializable(typeof(TicketResult))] internal sealed partial class TicketJsonContext : JsonSerializerContext; public static class SupportTools { [AgentTool( Description = "Creates a new customer support ticket", JsonContext = typeof(TicketJsonContext))] public static TicketResult CreateTicket( [Description("The ticket request")] SupportTicket request) { return new TicketResult(Id: 42, Status: "open"); } } Generated Code The source generator automatically generates: An ITool implementation (CreateTicketTool) wrapping the method. A compile-time constant string for ParametersSchemaJson containing the exact JSON schema of SupportTicket. An extension method SupportToolsAgentToolsExtensions.AsCreateTicketTool() for registration. // Register the compile-time tool directly assembly.Tools.Add(SupportToolsAgentToolsExtensions.AsCreateTicketTool());

docs/tool-approval.html.title: Tool Approval & Governance | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/tool-approval.html.summary: Tool Approval & Governance When AI agents invoke tools that interact with databases, payment gateways, or filesystem resources, safe governance is critical. Tool Approval Policies (IToolApprovalPolicy) Every tool call generated by a model passes through IToolApprovalPolicy before execution: using MyAgents.Core.Approvals; var policy = new RuleBasedToolApprovalPolicy() // Read-only tools are automatically allowed .AllowTool("get_current_time") .AllowTool("search_knowledge_base") // Sensitive tools require explicit confirmation .RequireApproval("delete_customer_record") .SetDefaultDecision(ToolApprovalDecision.Reject("policy", "Tool is not in allowlist.")); services.AddSingleton<IToolApprovalPolicy>(policy); Approval Decisions An IToolApprovalGate or policy can return: Allow: The tool executes immediately. Reject: The tool call is aborted, and a structured rejection message is returned to the model explaining the failure. RequiresApproval: Execution halts until an operator or approval gate provides an approval signal. Circuit Breaker Middleware Protect downstream APIs from infinite loops or rapid model retries using CircuitBreakerMiddleware: var circuitBreaker = new CircuitBreakerMiddleware(new CircuitBreakerOptions { FailureThreshold = 3, BreakDuration = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30) });

index.html.title: MyAgents Community | MyAgents Community Documentation
index.html.summary: MyAgents Community Build modular, tool-using AI agents with .NET 10. MyAgents Community is a modular, high-performance, and provider-neutral agent runtime for .NET 10. Connect any AI model through Microsoft.Extensions.AI's IChatClient, compose agent behaviors from reusable features, and execute tool invocations with NativeAOT safety, durable restart recovery, and hybrid memory retrieval. Quick Start (C#) using Microsoft.Extensions.AI; using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection; using MyAgents.Core; using MyAgents.Core.Tools; using MyAgents.Runtime.Chat; // 1. Configure services with your IChatClient and MyAgents runtime var services = new ServiceCollection(); services.AddSingleton<IChatClient>(chatClient); services.AddMyAgentsChatRuntime(); await using var provider = services.BuildServiceProvider(); var sessionFactory = provider.GetRequiredService<IAgentSessionFactory>(); // 2. Define an agent with system prompts and tools var definition = new AgentDefinition("assistant", [ AgentFeature.Create(assembly => { assembly.Prompts.AddSystem("You are a helpful assistant."); assembly.Tools.Add(DelegateTool.Create("get_time", () => DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.ToString("O"))); }) ]); // 3. Create a session and run turns await using var session = sessionFactory.CreateSession("session-1", definition); var turn = await session.InvokeAsync([AgentMessage.FromText("user", "What time is it in UTC?")]); foreach (var message in turn.Output) { Console.WriteLine(message.Content); } Read the Guides to explore NativeAOT tools, durable execution, and hybrid RAG memory.
